question: For the equality \(\frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x-2}}=\sqrt{\frac{x}{x-2}}\) to hold, the range of values of \(x\) is
solution: The radicand must satisfy \(x\geq 0\), and the radical \(\sqrt{x-2}\) in the denominator requires \(x-2>0\) (the denominator cannot be 0). Combining these conditions gives \(x>2\).
